classification: The existing contract enforces entry instantaneous voltage/power but not interval Coulombs. SOC clamping hides charge beyond the stored/free capacity. This increment intentionally tightens the supported held-operating-point interval domain; it does not claim a full within-cell electrochemical integration.
intended_contract: For the repository's positive-discharge convention, held current I over dt requests dQ_ah=I*dt/3600. Bounded stateful batteries require -((1-SOC)*Q) <= dQ_ah <= SOC*Q.
Reject nonfinite interval charge and current/capacity/SOC domain errors before any battery field is changed.

Allow only comparison roundoff of eight ULPs at the requested/available charge scale; do not use a physical Ah margin or capacity-scale absolute epsilon. Keep the existing endpoint clamp only for such representational boundary roundoff.

An interval crossing the charge boundary is unrepresentable by the current held-operating-point cell. Reject it; do not post-hoc clip DC power/current/energy while retaining the solved force and distance.

Provide a pure optional battery update preflight capability to preserve the existing structural BatteryModel protocol for third-party replacements. All three built-in batteries implement it; stateful update_state also enforces its own interval budget.

Vehicle computes battery terminal power without committing component/path state, runs supported battery preflight, then commits as before. Built-in rejected cells must leave full serialized state and telemetry unchanged.
Preserve the original force, motor/inverter conversion, current root, RC zero-order-hold update and all valid interval outputs. Ideal constant-power Battery intentionally has no finite Coulomb state.

No new adaptive subdivision, duration-aware force envelope, different driving controls, retuned voltage/OCV/RC parameters or raw model calibration is introduced. Callers may refine the cell or change controls after rejection.
planned_checks: Reproduce and reject both discharge exhaustion and charge overfill for OCVPackBattery and RCTheveninBattery; no partial state mutation.
At exact and adjacent charge boundaries, distinguish numerical roundoff from real excess; validate invalid dt and nonfinite charge cleanly.
Battery/vehicle P=VI, Coulomb accounting, throughput, motor/inverter/force consistency and accepted telemetry stay coherent.
Vehicle coarse-cell exhaustion and high-SOC regeneration overfill reject atomically before aero/path/component state commit.

Run original frozen2160case grid on baseline and repaired sources with8CPUworkers/native1thread; every newly rejected case is attributable to interval budget and every previously valid remaining output stays exact.
Retain the legacy battery protocol seam, test a third-party battery without the optional preflight and a pure preflight-capable rejection.
Independent practical review and appropriate focused/CI checks before a scoped draft stacked on PR15. Preserve all earlier heads/receipts.

primary_sources.use: SOC as capacity ratio and current integration; its current sign convention differs from this repo's explicitly positive discharge convention.
Coulomb accounting and remaining capacity; source also warns capacity/initial-state/measurement uncertainty matters in real systems.
Primary research distinguishes current measurement, integration, capacity and timing errors; no claim that this bound repairs those real-world uncertainties.

policy_attribution: The conservative whole-interval rejection is an implementation choice inferred from the existing held-point model and charge balance, not a rule mandated by the references.
excluded_claims: No real battery capacity or car calibration
No continuous SOC/voltage feasibility over an accepted coarse cell
No firmware, hardware, CAN, deployment, target timing or safety certification
